tasks.title: Linear BEC heating
tasks.statement: A linear regulator steps **{vin} V** down to **{vout} V** at a current of **{i} A**. How many watts does it dissipate?
tasks.solution: P = (U_in − U_out)·I. That is why a linear BEC from 6S (22.2 V nominal) to 5 V at 1 A means ~17 W of heat (~20 W from a full charge, 25.2 V); you need a switching one.

tasks.title: Switching BEC input current
tasks.statement: A switching BEC with an efficiency of **{eta} %** delivers **{vout} V** at **{i} A** from a **{vin} V** bus. What current does it draw from the bus (A)?

tasks.title: Drop across the power lead
tasks.statement: A power lead of **{r} mΩ/m** (5.21 is 12 AWG, 8.28 is 14 AWG, 13.17 is 16 AWG), plus and minus **{l} cm** each, peak current **{i} A**. Find the voltage drop across the lead (V).
tasks.solution: The current flows through the plus and back through the minus: the loop length is 2·l. ΔU = I·R'·2l. The module's example: 14 AWG, 2 × 15 cm, 80 A → 80 × 0.00828 × 0.3 = 0.199 V (0.9 % of 22.2 V).

tasks.title: LC filter resonance
tasks.statement: Video LC filter: a **{l} µH** inductor, a **{c} µF** capacitor. Find the resonance frequency f₀ (Hz).
tasks.solution: f₀ = 1/(2π√(LC)). Above f₀ the filter attenuates at 40 dB/decade; at f₀ itself it amplifies by Q = √(L/C)/(DCR + ESR). The module's example: 22 µH and 470 µF → 1565 Hz.

tasks.title: Precharge time (antispark)
tasks.statement: A power bus with a capacitance of **{c} µF** charges through a **{r} Ω** precharge resistor. After how many milliseconds (5τ) is the capacitor 99 % charged so that the main contact can close?
tasks.solution: τ = R·C; after 5τ the voltage reaches 1 − e⁻⁵ = 99.3 %. The module's example: 10 Ω × 1040 µF = 10.4 ms, 5τ = 52 ms. The peak current U/R and the peak power U²/R determine the choice of a pulse-rated resistor.
